notes.short: Believers' death is called falling asleep
notes.about: Paul says that Jesus died; believers who have died he calls those who have fallen asleep in Him. Death is named gently as sleep, for God will bring them with Jesus: for those in Him, death will end in rising, as sleep ends in waking.

figure.name: Euphemism
figure.means: died: death spoken of gently, as a sleep from which God will raise them

original.note: In Paul's Greek the word for Jesus is apethanen, died; for believers it is koimēthentes, laid to sleep.

notes.evidence: Bullinger lists the verse under Euphemy: God calls His people asleep, since the Lord will come to wake them. Fausset (Jamieson, Fausset and Brown) notes that death is said of Christ but sleep of believers. A. J. Mason (Ellicott) finds the metaphor of sleep sweetening the phrase. Barnes calls it a most beautiful expression for rest in hope of waking; Calvin and Clarke read it as death in Christ.
notes.limit: Some take the word sleep as set on purpose against the word died used of Jesus. The note does not take the sleep to mean that the dead know nothing until the resurrection.

cites.quote: in the case of His own people, He speaks of their being “put to sleep by Jesus” (1Th 4:14 ). It is only a “sleep”; because the Lord Himself will come to wake them.

cites.quote: He died and then rose: so believers shall die and then rise with Him. But in His case death is the term used, Co1 15:3 , Co1 15:6 , &c.; in theirs, sleep; because His death has taken for them the sting from death.

cites.quote: Additional sweetness is imparted to the phrase by the use of the metaphor of sleep

cites.quote: To sleep in Christ, is to retain in death the connection that we have with Christ, for those that are by faith ingrafted into Christ, have death in common with him, that they may be partakers with him of life.

Which sleep in Jesus - A most beautiful expression. It is not merely that they have calm repose - like a gentle slumber - in the hope of awaking again ... Such is the sleep of our pious friends now in the grave; such will be our own when we die.
